data.name: Akfah
data.gender_notes: Akfah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Arabic word 'akfah', meaning 'to seek knowledge'. It is a name with spiritual significance, emphasizing the importance of education and wisdom in Islamic culture. The name Akfah carries the meaning “Seeking Knowledge” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Akfah usually hope their child will grow to embody seeking knowledge and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes a lifelong pursuit of knowledge and wisdom.
data.etymology: Akfah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Seeking Knowledge.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Akfah total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: أكفاه
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم مشتق من أَكْفَى، وهو من الأفعال التي تعني كفاية الله تعالى لعبده من كل مكروه أو سوء، ويوحي بالتوكل على الله والاعتماد عليه في جميع الأمور. ورد في القرآن الكريم في عدة مواضع، منها قول الله تعالى: «وَكَفَينَاكَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ» (الأحزاب: 25)، أي كفاك الله منهم شرهم.

in_urdu.name: اکفاہ
in_urdu.long_meaning: اس نام کا مطلب ہے اللہ کی طرف سے کفایت، یعنی اللہ کی رضا اور مدد پر بھروسہ کرنا۔ یہ نام عربی جڑوں سے ماخوذ ہے، جہاں لفظ 'کفا' کا مطلب ہے کافی ہونا یا مطمئن ہونا۔ اردو بولنے والے مسلمانوں میں اس کا استعمال ایک ایسے بچے کے لیے کیا جاتا ہے جس کے لیے اللہ کی کفایت کافی ہے۔

in_hindi.name: अकफाह
in_hindi.long_meaning: यह नाम अरबी मूल से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है भगवान से पर्याप्त। यह नाम भगवान पर भरोसा और निर्भरता की भावना को दर्शाता है। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, यह नाम एक ऐसे बच्चे के लिए चुना जाता है जिसे भगवान की कृपा और समर्थन की आवश्यकता होती है।

in_pashto.name: اکفاه
in_pashto.long_meaning: دا نوم د الله له کفايت څخه مشتق شوی دی، يعنی الله تعالی د خپل بند څخه د هر ډول شر یا بدۍ څخه کفايت کوي. دا نوم د پښتنو د کلتور او دود سره تړاو لري، چیرې چې د الله تعالی پر توکل او د هغه د رضا او مدد پر باوري ټینګار شوی دی.

in_english.name: Akfah
in_english.long_meaning: The name Akfah originates from Arabic roots, specifically from the term 'kafā' which means to suffice or be enough. In Islamic context, it signifies being content with Allah's providence and relying on Him. The Quran mentions similar concepts in various verses, emphasizing trust and satisfaction with divine will.

data.cultural_impact: The name Akfah is deeply rooted in the Islamic tradition that values education and knowledge. It encourages and motivates the bearer to seek knowledge and wisdom, which are considered essential for personal growth and development. In Islamic society, learning and applying knowledge are highly regarded, as it is believed to be a means to understand the divine and lead a purposeful life.
data.spiritual_significance: Akfah carries a deeper spiritual significance, reminding the bearer of the importance of seeking knowledge and wisdom not just for material gain but also for the advancement of the soul. It is seen as a reflection of the belief that knowledge is a gift from God and that it is our responsibility to utilize it for the betterment of ourselves and others. This name also serves as a reminder of the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) words, "Seeking knowledge is a duty imposed on every Muslim." (Bukhari and Muslim)

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun describes Akfah as an important agricultural and commercial center during the 14th century in his book 'The Muqaddimah'. It was strategically located at the crossroads of major trade routes between the Mediterranean, the Red Sea, and the Sahara desert.
historical_references.context: Important city in Maghreb, North Africa

historical_references.reference: Al-Idrisi, in his 12th century geography book 'Nuzhat al-mushtaq fi ikhbat al-amakin', mentions Akfah as a significant port city on the eastern coast of the Mediterranean Sea, known for its production of olive oil and salt.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Islamic term 'Akfah' refers to a charitable donation for the purpose of seeking knowledge. In the modern context, the term has been reinterpreted to include various initiatives aimed at promoting sustainable agriculture, eco-tourism, and community development. On platforms such as Instagram, individuals and organizations share visual content showcasing their agricultural projects and eco-friendly practices. On Facebook, groups and pages are dedicated to discussing and sharing information related to these initiatives. On YouTube, educational videos and documentaries provide insight into the processes and impacts of sustainable agriculture and eco-tourism projects. These trends reflect the growing importance of environmental stewardship and community engagement in the Islamic world and beyond.

name_in_real_life.story: A successful entrepreneur named Maryam Akfah in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia attributes much of their success to the blessing of their name Akfah, which means "Seeking Knowledge". They believe their name has shaped their identity and guided them through life.
